mouthpiece: Tenor or tenor/bass mp,³  17c; made in 2 parts, a bored head and a soldered cylindrical tube; diam of bowl 23.4; throat 7.4, outlet 10.6, depth of bowl 14.7; total length 110.3; rim 6.3

literature: Kinsky 1913:199; Sachs 1922: col. 229; Wörthmüller 1955: 402-03; Heyde 1980a: 185-86, tafel 25, 40, 44, 47 (photos); Langwill 1980: 14; Fischer 1984: 45; Myers A 1998; Lane 1982: 183.
remarks: Exceptional workmanship, good condition. 16 ferrules with dragon-scale pattern: 6 in bell sec., 10 similar ones at slide-stays. 6 pos.; bell in vicinity of 3rd pos.; ball or knob with crown-like garnishes and vertical striations in bell sec. Flat immoveable slide-stay, with dragon-head clasps, engraved with pomegranate, and in middle, a star. Tubular moveable slide-stay, with plain hinged handle attached. Ring in slide-bow, bell-bow. Flat bell-stay, with hinge on bell-pipe side, polygonal sleeve decorated with striped pattern on neck-pipe side; bell-stay engraved with angel playing a cornett on upper surface, on reverse side a winged form with a harp, on the borders, engraved scroll-like forms. In bell-pipe a large knurled ball or knob, slotted, attached to bell-pipe with sleeves in notched pattern.
